correctness.rationale: Under endpoint-uniform sampling, the unoriented line angle is uniform on [0,pi) and signed offset has density [pi sqrt(1-s²)]^{-1}; integrating intersection offsets between x·n and y·n gives the claimed arcsine-difference integral /pi². Positive line separation yields strict triangle inequality unless a point lies on the Euclidean segment, so segments are precisely unparametrized minimizing geodesics. Differentiation for interior x gives F_x(v), with smooth strictly convex co-unit curve from h+h''=2/(pi² sqrt(1-(x·n_perp)²))>0. Direct integration yields F_radial=2 artanh(r)/(pi² r), F_tangent=2 arcsin(r)/(pi² r); derivative of arcsin(r)-sqrt(1-r²)artanh(r) is r artanh(r)/sqrt(1-r²)>0, proving strict radial ratio recovery. An ellipse support h would have (h+h'')^{-2/3} affine in sin² theta, contradicting its actual nonaffine cube-root dependence away from zero. Radial integral gives odd dilogarithm and distance 1/4 at boundary; pairs of boundary endpoints give alpha(2pi-alpha)/(2pi²). Continuous compact completion is closed disk, and any completed isometry agrees on the metric boundary with O(2), fixes the unique radial midpoint and all straight radial geodesics. Independent numeric quadrature checked radial/tangent formulas for r=.1,.5,.9, not used as proof.
